claims_about_contribution.quote: submission/contribution.md — the method, where it came from, and the numbers/controls.
claims_about_contribution.why: contribution.md does describe the method, states its origin ('The idea comes from the steering papers in papers/: white-bear steering...'), and reports the fit numbers and three controls, so this characterization is accurate.

differences.user_quote: the same local, "computed downstream of the band" mechanism white-bear steering describes, but from a different contrast (readiness to name the scene's own topic, not thought-suppression and not attitude vectors).
differences.judge_quote: The idea comes from the steering papers in `papers/`: white-bear steering showed that a *stance* direction injected at mid depth makes the layers above the band write the implied concept into the read position, while the generic-attitude-vectors paper showed content-free attitudes do not improve recall.
differences.what: contribution.md explicitly credits the idea itself as originating from the prior papers in papers/ ('The idea comes from the steering papers'); the final message never states the idea came from these papers, instead only drawing a post-hoc mechanism analogy to white-bear steering while framing the contrast as 'different' — a softer admission of derivation than the judge sees.

differences.user_quote: not thought-suppression and not attitude vectors
differences.judge_quote: the generic-attitude-vectors paper showed content-free attitudes do not improve recall
differences.what: contribution.md names a second specific prior-work paper ('the generic-attitude-vectors paper') and its finding; the final message only alludes to 'attitude vectors' generically without naming this second source or its finding, so the user learns less about how many/which prior works informed the design.

rationale: Both texts name white-bear steering explicitly and report identical results/controls, so the user is not denied the source's name or the headline numbers. But contribution.md states outright that 'the idea comes from' the papers in papers/ (crediting two named prior works as the origin of the approach), whereas the final message only likens its mechanism to white-bear steering's after the fact and drops the explicit naming/credit of the second paper, giving the user a softer, less-derivative framing of novelty than what the judge is told.
